entries.source: Knowledge work rarely arrives as a neat plan. It starts as an observation, a question, or a half-formed thought. In IOTHS, that thought can stay a note until a few checkboxes reveal work worth doing.

entries.source: The app does not pretend to predict what happens next. It gives the work somewhere calm to change shape: a note becomes a checklist, a checklist becomes active work, and the board shows the pattern that is already there.

entries.source: Your notes stay on this device until you explicitly turn on a sync destination. There's no IOTHS account and no developer-operated sign-in. Usage analytics are off unless you turn them on, and even then they never include note content, titles, or tags. Nothing is sold. Nothing trains an AI model. Read the full Privacy Policy.

entries.source: Why this exists
entries.context: H2 content. Preserve any inline HTML tags and attributes.

entries.source: I built IOTHS for myself, first. I'd never found a notes app that actually fit — not functionally, not in how it felt to use — so I made the one I wanted. That's where it started: not to monetize it, not to be seen. Just to have it.
entries.context: P content. Preserve any inline HTML tags and attributes.

entries.source: The icon is a small nod to Conway's Game of Life and complexity theory: simple local rules, surprising patterns. It is a familiar way to think about emergence in complex adaptive systems, not a claim that IOTHS models them. IOTHS is simply a place where a thought can stay small until the work asks for more structure.
